    Each game has storylines significant enough to fill any plate. To keep up with everything, we've provided a rundown of how to follow the games in real time. We've also included the major thing to know for each matchup.

    Industry observers note that what to know: While he's had a lot of success in Chicago, Ben Johnson is 0-2 against Detroit, his former team. Johnson's former boss, Dan Campbell, has won four straight games against Chicago, seven of his last eight in the series and has a 7-3 overall record against the Bears.

    Coaches aside, this is a matchup between two of the NFL's hottest teams. The Bears have won five straight games, while the Lions enter Thursday with a six-game winning streak. The winner of this game will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North.

    It has been revealed that it'll be especially interesting when the Lions' fifth-ranked offense is on the field against Chicago's sixth-ranked defense. Jahmyr Gibbs, who is one touchdown away from breaking Barry Sanders' NFL record for the most touchdowns by a player before his 25th birthday, should have his moments. He's facing a run defense that is just 25th in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed.

    What to know: Dallas is a sizable favorite, but there are several reasons to believe that the Eagles are ripe for an upset.

    According to recent reports, the Cowboys were 10-point favorites when they were upset by then-winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers back in Week 5. Dallas lost that game to a backup quarterback (rookie Jalon Daniels), and they'll face another backup Thursday in Joe Milton III, who used to play for America's Team. Milton just won his first career start Sunday against the Steelers. He made several clutch plays, including his third-down conversion to DeVonta Smith that iced the game.

    Industry observers note that if Dallas wins on Thursday, it will be the first time it's won back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys' inability to string together consecutive wins is yet another reason why Philadelphia could successfully play the role of spoiler.

    What to know: This game will be billed as the latest chapter in the Josh Allen-Patrick Mahomes rivalry. Overall, the Allen-Mahomes series is tied up at five wins apiece, which makes Thursday night's game a rubber match. Allen is 0-4 against Mahomes-led teams in the playoffs, but he has a 5-1 record in regular-season starts against Mahomes that includes five straight victories.

    Recent findings suggest that both quarterbacks will look to put on a show, but the winner of this game will likely come down to which supporting cast outperforms the other. On paper, the Chiefs have a few advantages, most notably their second-ranked scoring defense that will look to exploit Allen's Kryptonite: turning the ball over. Allen has thrown nine interceptions this year, including five in his last four games.

    It'll be interesting to see how the Chiefs' young players fare in a major-time environment, especially Emmett Johnson, Kansas City's rookie running back, who has tallied consecutive 100-yard rushing performances while filling in for injured starter Kenneth Walker III.

    According to recent reports, what to know: This game is pretty simple. If the Steelers are going to pull off an upset, they're going to have to take advantage of Denver's suspect run defense and third-down offense. If they can't do either of those things, the Broncos will more than likely hand them their third straight loss.

    Jaylen Warren was having a monster season for Pittsburgh until he and the rest of the Steelers' offense hit a wall over the last two weeks. Pittsburgh's lack of depth at receiver has led defenses to crowd the line of scrimmage, leaving little running room for Warren and back mate Rico Dowdle.

    According to recent reports, A positive for Pittsburgh is the emergence of wideout Max Hurleman, who caught a team-high six passes for 61 yards and a score against the Eagles. Plus, the recent return of Roman Wilson and the possible return of Michael Pittman, who hasn't played since Week 4, are bright spots. The Steelers will also have DK Metcalf after the league decided not to suspend him following his ejection during Sunday's loss in Philadelphia.

    #210925. Winners and losers of the Tarik Skubal signing: Blue Jays, Dodgers strike out; David Stearns looks nervous

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (759 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Winners and losers of the Tarik Skubal signing: Blue Jays, Dodgers strike out; David Stearns looks nervous

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The best player in a thin free agent class came off the board Sunday evening.
    • The $450 million contract shatters the previous record for a pitcher, which is Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million contract with the Dodgers, Skubal's most recent team.
    • Here now are our winners and losers from Skubal's monster contract with the Mets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The best player in a thin free agent class came off the board Sunday evening. Two-time Cy Young winning left-hander Tarik Skubal has agreed to a record nine-year, $450 million contract with the New York Mets. There's a $45 million signing bonus and $30 million in deferred payments. The team has not yet announced the signing but that should happen soon.

    The $450 million contract shatters the previous record for a pitcher, which is Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million contract with the Dodgers, Skubal's most recent team. The $50 million average annual salary also shatters the previous record for a pitcher. That was $43.3 million for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander during their time with the Mets.

    Here now are our winners and losers from Skubal's monster contract with the Mets.

    Let's start with the obvious: Skubal's a winner because he signed a massive, record-shattering contract. Sign a record deal and you're always a winner in my book. The Mets are a winner because they landed not just the best free agent on the market, but one of the game's best pitchers. Skubal is a power player who can swing a postseason race or a postseason series all by himself. There are very few players like that in the game and now the Mets have one to lead their rotation.

    Recent findings suggest that boras, Skubal's agent, tends to shatter records, not beat them by just a little bit. Alex Rodriguez's contract with the Rangers is his Mona Lisa: A-Rod's $252 million contract was exactly double the largest contract in the four major North American sports leagues at the time (Kevin Garnett's $126 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves). Boras did it again with Skubal. He obliterated Yamamoto's total guarantee record, Scherzer's and Verlander's shared average annual value record, and also Max Fried's record deal for a lefty ($218 million). Once again, Boras won substantial.

    We can add the Padres here too since they were one of the four teams to meet with Skubal in person this past week, though it was always hard to see San Diego beating out the Blue Jays, Dodgers, and Mets. The Dodgers reportedly held the line at a short-term, high-dollar contract similar to Kyle Tucker's deal, which put them at a disadvantage. Still, they no longer have Skubal in their rotation, and he's irreplaceable. The Blue Jays have been trying to sign top free agents for years (Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Juan Soto, etc.) and have yet to land the plane. Point is, these teams met and pursued Skubal, then he signed elsewhere. Ergo, losers.

    Sources indicate that with Skubal off the board, the market for second- and third-tier free agent starters should quickly pick up. That group includes Michael King, Freddy Peralta, and Trevor Rogers. Skubal signing this early is a massive win for everyone, really, and especially the other free agent starters. They have more than a week to negotiate and sign before the owners are expected to lock out the players after the current CBA expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1. Pitchers are coming off the board fast and furious right now. Expect that to continue for another week or so.

    To be sure, the Mets' president of baseball operations is a winner because his team now employs Skubal. This is 100% a Steve Cohen contract, though. Stearns has been against long-term contracts for pitchers throughout his career as an executive, even if he mentioned during the GM Meetings that he works on a "case-by-case basis," and it's hard to believe he'd give a pitcher with three elbow surgeries on his resume this contract. It seems likely Cohen was the one pushing this deal across the finish line, and hey, he's the owner; he can do whatever he wants. Stearns is very much against long-term deals for pitchers, though. I imagine he feels at least a wee bit nervous. Plus, he really can't afford another disaster season like 2026.

    In a recent development, once again, the top free agent went with a significant market team. The Mets are signing Skubal this offseason. The Dodgers signed Tucker last offseason. The Mets signed Soto the offseason before that. The Dodgers signed Ohtani the offseason before that. The folks who insist baseball needs a salary cap, both the owners themselves and the fans who lean that way, now have more ammunition for their fight. Settle in. It is very, very likely we're in for months of salary cap debate during an extended lockout. That was true even before Skubal signed.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (5-6) have the chance to do something they haven't done yet in the 2026 season against the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving Day: win consecutive games.
    • Sources indicate that the only time the Cowboys have won back-to-back games under head coach Brian Schottenheimer came back in his first season in 2025 following their Week 10 bye.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (5-6) have the chance to do something they haven't done yet in the 2026 season against the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving Day: win consecutive games.

    Sources indicate that the only time the Cowboys have won back-to-back games under head coach Brian Schottenheimer came back in his first season in 2025 following their Week 10 bye. That was a stretch of three victories in a row against Las Vegas Raiders (33-16), the Eagles (24-21) and the Kansas City Chiefs (31-28) on Thanksgiving Day.

    Sources indicate that after Dallas' 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans (1-9) on Sunday, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones has some hope that his squad can make a postseason push down the stretch. That's just days after Jones called his Cowboys "a bad team" in the wake of their 46-40 home loss against the San Francisco 49ers (9-1) in Week 10.

    Recent findings suggest that "It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we wanted to do," Jones said postgame on Sunday. "We needed this kind of thing. Any team does. We needed to feel it and get a little wind under our wings, so to speak.".

    Recent findings suggest that quarterback Dak Prescott looks to continue his high-level play on Thanksgiving. If he replicated his Sunday performance against the Titans (325 yards passing and four touchdowns on 28-of-33 passing with a rushing touchdown), that would give Prescott 19 passing touchdowns on Thanksgiving, the record for the most Thanksgiving Day touchdowns in NFL history. Prescott's predecessor Tony Romo and Matthew Stafford right now share the record with 18 Turkey Day passing touchdowns each.

    "It's a blessing. It's something that, one of my favorite games of the year," Prescott stated Tuesday. "And so, just being able to put that uniform on with the John Madden seal on it, understanding the whole world's watching and how many little kids are in the position that I once was: watching the game and then ready to go outside and play my own version of it. ... I don't take it for granted.".

    However, there's one Cowboy who doesn't look forward to Thanksgiving: defensive tackle Quinnen Williams. The four-time Pro Bowler doesn't enjoy the holiday because it goes against his in-season training and diet regimen. Williams' go-to Thanksgiving side dish is macaroni, something that is hard to resist this time of year.

    Sources indicate that "It's during the season. I'm trying to stay lean and trim, and it's a holiday right around when real football starts to come in," stated Williams. "So I'm not a big fan of Thanksgiving.".

    Recent findings suggest that that's okay, because there will be plenty of fans ready to see Williams on the field, especially against starting Eagles quarterback and former Cowboy Joe Milton. Dallas acquired Milton in a trade with the New England Patriots in April 2025, and he worked as one of Prescott's backups until the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 17. That's the same day Philadelphia placed Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) on injured reserve.

    Sources indicate that "Haha, it's good to see him," said Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb. "I hope he don't go crazy.".

    Prescott is cooking right now. He became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club. After racking up 1,003 yards passing, 11 touchdowns and just a single interception over the last three weeks, Prescott now ranks second in the league in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25). He also ranks eighth in touchdown-to-interception ratio (25-6) and passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21) this season.

    Prescott credited his historic production to being able to play "balanced football" the last two weeks, with the Cowboys averaging the 12th-most rushing yards per game (125.5) since Week 10.

    "It really just opens up the whole playbook," Prescott said Thursday. "So it's a credit to all of it just, in that sense, coming together. Guys up front being physical in the run game, which then allows them to pass block a little bit easier there. And guys outside just getting open, making my job easier.".

    Industry observers note that in their 51-30 Week 11 win over the Titans, Schottenheimer provided Prescott and Co. their highest motion rate (63.5%) and play-action rate (58.3%) of the season, weeks after getting away from those staples through the first quarter of the year.

    In a recent development, cowboys Pro Bowl wide receivers Lamb (1,108 receiving yards, the second most in the NFL) and George Pickens (780 receiving yards, the 11th most in the NFL) going up against the Eagles All-Pro cornerback tandem of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean will be the key matchups on Thursday. However, Mitchell's status was uncertain because of a hamstring injury. The Eagles held walkthroughs on Monday and Tuesday, and they upgraded Mitchell to limited on Tuesday after he didn't participate on Monday.

    Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Mitchell will be "fine" for Thanksgiving, and the Eagles listed him without a game status on the team's final injury report after he practiced fully on Wednesday, indicating he will indeed play.

    Industry observers note that when the Eagles have the football, they'll definitely be looking to play ground-and-pound football with 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley. Barkley is currently on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career. The Cowboys have the worst run defense in football, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per game, and they struggle against Barkley's agile running style.

    Both Schottenheimer and Williams described Barkley as being a "jump cut" running back with how smoothly he can hit the hole and then glide to a different spot along the line of scrimmage and in the open field. Williams compared Barkley stylistically to Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving, who went off for 165 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in a 24-16 upset over the Cowboys in Week 5. Irving averaged a career-high 7.9 yards per carry that night at AT&T Stadium. Williams stated the key is to stop Barkley's feet before he gets going.

    Williams also presents a challenge for Philadelphia as he leads the NFL with 18 tackles for loss, the most in a season by a defensive tackle since 2022. He also leads all defensive tackles in quarterback pressures (40) and co-leads his position in forced fumbles (4) along with Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter. Yet, he feels he can still find higher levels of play with the Cowboys defense allowing 20-plus points in 18 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. That's the longest such streak since the 2019-2021 Jacksonville Jaguars' run of 25 straight games, per NFL Research.

    Milton earned his first career win as an NFL starting quarterback on Sunday in the Eagles' 19-16 home victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers that snapped the team's seven-game losing streak. He completed 11 of his 21 throws for 141 passing yards while rushing for 7 yards on five carries. Prescott noted he saw Milton develop most in Dallas on his mental side of the game and preparation as it pertains to pass protection adjustments and discernment at the line of scrimmage.

    In a recent development, "Joe is amazing, man. The athleticism that he has, the speed that he has, the arm talent that he has, he can do it all," Williams remarked. "So it's super dope to be able to go against him, especially after all the laughs and things we had in the locker room during training camp practices.".

    In a recent development, the present iteration of the Eagles lacks the offensive artillery to win a duel with Prescott, Lamb and Pickens. That's especially true if Mitchell is unable to suit up on Thursday. Prescott is on a 20-game home winning streak against NFC East opponents, which is tied with Tom Brady (versus the AFC East) for the longest home winning streak by a starting quarterback against divisional opponents since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. He'll break the tie with Brady with his 21st such victory in a row on Thanksgiving.

    #210922. Latest Update: Timberwolves, Grizzlies reportedly hope to move to Eastern Conference after expansion; who makes more sense?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1430 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Timberwolves, Grizzlies reportedly hope to move to Eastern Conference after expansion; who makes more sense?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1430 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The NBA is barreling toward expansion, and the addition of two upcoming teams would have enormous basketball implications for the remaining 30.
    • In a recent development, several teams are eager to do so, according to The Athletic.
    • Getting out of the West would be appealing on several levels.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NBA is barreling toward expansion, and the addition of two upcoming teams would have enormous basketball implications for the remaining 30. Perhaps the biggest is geographic. Both Seattle and Las Vegas are located firmly in the western half of the United States. Should those cities eventually be granted teams, they would play in the Western Conference, leaving the league with unbalanced conferences. Therefore, someone in the West would have to move to the East in order to balance the conferences at 16 teams apiece.

    In a recent development, several teams are eager to do so, according to The Athletic. While the Fresh Orleans Pelicans are not out of the running, the likeliest teams to move in realignment, for now, are reportedly the Minnesota Timberwolves and Memphis Grizzlies.

    Getting out of the West would be appealing on several levels. Of course, there are obvious basketball reasons for preferring the East. Putting aside the decades of Western Conference superiority that hold little weight in the long run, the two teams best positioned to succeed over the next decade or so are the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder. As the New York Knicks learned last June, the easiest path to a championship is avoiding Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander until they've already spent seven games battling each other.

    It has been revealed that but this isn't just a basketball conversation. The NBA, like most major American professional sports leagues, tilts east. There are simply more major cities in the Eastern half of the country than the Western half. Of the league's 30 existing teams, 17 play east of the Mississippi River: the 15 already in the Eastern Conference, along with the Timberwolves and Grizzlies.

    Sources indicate that travel is simply easier playing in the East. One projection of how many total miles each NBA team will travel this season has only the Miami Heat in the top half of the league, with the other 14 slots belonging to Western Conference teams. That projection has the Heat crossing 24 time zones, while every Western Conference team crosses at least 36.

    So Minnesota, Memphis and Fresh Orleans are all incentivized to move, and with the Grizzlies and Timberwolves seemingly favored, let's evaluate the cases for each.

    The fundamental case for the Grizzlies is geographic. Memphis is further East than Minneapolis. As The Athletic points out, it is closer to more Eastern Conference teams as well, as it is within 600 miles of five East teams (Charlotte Hornets, Atlanta Hawks, Indiana Pacers, Chicago Bulls and Milwaukee Bucks). This not only makes travel easier for the Grizzlies, but for those teams as well.

    While the Timberwolves are considered the better team right now, Memphis is probably the team better positioned to be competitive in the long run. Minnesota's best players -- Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu -- are all in their mid-20s earning market-rate salaries, and Rudy Gobert is much older at 34. Plus, the Timberwolves are essentially devoid of first-round draft capital.

    The Grizzlies have a significant draft surplus, and their best players -- Cameron Boozer, Cedric Coward and Zach Edey -- are still on their rookie deals. If the idea is balancing the two conferences competitively, even if the Timberwolves have a higher immediate upside, the Grizzlies are probably the team we should expect to contend longer.

    And then there's the matter of maintaining established rivalries. While neither the Grizzlies nor the Timberwolves are franchises steeped in historical success, Minnesota's last few years have established the Timberwolves as genuine postseason rivals to several important Western Conference teams. They've faced Nikola Jokiċ and the Denver Nuggets in multiple recent playoff series. They've faced Luka Dončić in multiple recent playoff series, even if they've come against different teams. Their series against the Spurs last spring included a Wembanyama ejection.

    Sources indicate that the NBA may prefer to maximize the number of games Edwards plays against these high-profile opponents because there are existing narratives surrounding those matchups. In that case, keeping the Timberwolves in the West makes sense while allowing the Grizzlies to shift to the East.

    Minnesota's geographic case is a bit more nuanced. While Memphis is closer to more teams, Minnesota is closer to a few geographically convenient ones. If we assume for the moment that the fresh, 16-team conferences are going to come with four divisions featuring four teams each, Minnesota's proximity to Milwaukee, Chicago and Indiana makes for an easy four-team pod.

    The rest of the conference becomes remarkably easy to group from there. We have three more roughly Midwestern teams (Cleveland, Toronto and Detroit), five in the Northeast (Latest York, Brooklyn, Boston, Philadelphia and Washington) and four in the Southeast (Charlotte, Miami, Orlando and Atlanta). Just move one of those Northeastern teams to the Midwestern group -- presumably Washington, as it doesn't play in the existing Atlantic Division -- and you're set. If the NBA wants to make divisions a more prominent part of scheduling moving forward, Minnesota makes doing so much easier.

    Sources indicate that there's also the idea of giving Edwards, one of the league's more personable stars, an easier path to the NBA Finals by getting him away from Wembanyama and Gilgeous-Alexander. The NBA is, ultimately, a star business, and if stacking the deck in Edwards' favor helps build him up as one of the faces of the league, there is obvious appeal in doing so.

    In a recent development, by all accounts, we are far closer to resolution on a Las Vegas team than to the return of the Sonics in Seattle. Bidding has seemingly been more robust in Las Vegas, and an announcement is expected in the near future. If an announcement on Vegas comes before one in Seattle, there will be a brief period in which the NBA has an odd number of planned franchises.

    According to recent reports, that does not mean that it will ever actually play a season with only 31 teams. Seattle, as commissioner Adam Silver has described, is much more of a turnkey operation than Las Vegas because of its arena situation and preexisting basketball history. In theory, a Seattle team could be announced much later than a Las Vegas team and still begin play in the same season. For now, the reported target for expansion teams to tip off is the 2028-29 season. However, if Seattle's bidding process takes too long for the two to begin play at the same time, or worse, if no Seattle group manages to put forth an acceptable bid in the near future, the possibility of one or even multiple seasons with 31 teams rather than the expected 32 probably does exist.

    The NBA -- and every other major American professional sports league -- has had unbalanced conferences in the past. None do now. It creates scheduling headaches, and it's just blatantly unfair. Forcing some teams to overcome 15 opponents to reach the Finals while others only have to top 14 makes playing in the smaller conference too much of an advantage, and since the conference presently believed to be the superior one (the West) would be getting the Las Vegas team, competitive balance would go from a problem to an outright crisis.

    Fans have been calling for the abolition of conferences for decades now. Getting it to actually pass a vote would be harder. Realignment is voted on by the board of governors, so abolishing the conferences theoretically would be as well. Eastern Conference owners love having an easier path to the playoffs and the gate revenue those postseason games generate. This is where the idea of a season or two with just 31 teams in the league carries some appeal. It could give the NBA an opportunity to test the abolition of conferences provisionally with the idea that conferences would return when the league reaches 32 unless a new vote determines otherwise.

    The appeal of removing conferences altogether stems from the inherent fairness of a playoff system determined solely by record. There have been concerns about how removing the geographic component of playoff scheduling would affect travel, but there are potential solutions there. Returning to the "2-3-2" home-court format would minimize travel, or higher seeds could be allowed to select opponents in the early rounds to decide for themselves how they'd like to prioritize travel. The odds are obviously against the removal of conferences altogether, but expansion offers a potential opportunity to test it without committing to it long-term, and that's an opportunity the NBA would be foolish not to at least explore.

    Industry observers note that the Latest York Mets' splash record signing of ace lefty Tarik Skubal, who was far and away the top free agent available, has of course reset the market in a major way. Those who missed out on Skubal and those aspiring contenders who otherwise have rotation needs may be left wondering: What's next?

    Clubs like the Chicago Cubs, Atlanta Braves, San Diego Padres, Los Angeles Dodgers, Chicago White Sox, Tampa Bay Rays, among others, still have options, even if none of them rise to the skyscraping level of Mr. Skubal. Let's explore some possibilities for you, and let's also move beyond just the current class of free agents and name-check some potential trade targets who could buttress a rotation for next season and beyond. Let's jump in.

    Yes, Morejon is a reliever at this writing, but his deep repertoire, excellent velocity and stuff make him a compelling transition candidate for next season, even with recent reporting that he wants to stay in the bullpen. Morejon, who sits triple digits, can give some velocity back while working longer outings and still have plenty in the tank to miss bats in the strike zone. And if starting doesn't work, he can go right back to dominating as a reliever. He doesn't turn 28 until February.

    Recent findings suggest that while his ERA ballooned last season thanks to some early season struggles, Rogers' underlying performance indicators are still quite strong, specifically his ability to get chase out of the zone and duck quality contact with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years. He's not a name that leaps readily to mind, but Rogers has a high ceiling and bargain potential.

    Peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the Fresh York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter, all the way to ALCS MVP. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form. The 2027 season will be his age-31 campaign.

    He has a full, five-pitch repertoire with elite spin and movement on almost all of those five offerings and boasts an ERA+ of 129 for his career. King turns 32 in May, and he's experienced a gradual decline at the command-and-control level over the past few seasons. As well, his fastball's not beating hitters in the zone like it used to. That's to say, there's risk here, but even if he's beginning his decline phase, King will be a rotation asset for the near- to mid-term.

    Recent findings suggest that the 32-year-old righty was reborn last season after a deadline trade to the Braves. Atlanta ramped up his splitter usage and adjusted his slider shape, and in perhaps related matters, Mahle was much more successful at staying away from the heart of the zone. In 54 ⅓ innings after the trade, Mahle ran a sub-2.00 ERA and struck out 48 batters against nine walks. No, he's not going to put up those numbers over the long haul, but his revival makes him an intriguing option.

    Recent findings suggest that the big pre-Skubal hot stove news was the San Francisco Giants' reported willingness to listen to offers on ace Logan Webb. Webb, who just recently turned 30, endured a bit of a down 2026 on the run-prevention front, but the overall body of work remains very strong. For his career, the three-time All-Star has a career ERA+ of 115 with three top 10 finishes in the American League Cy Young vote. In three of the past four seasons, he's topped 200 innings. Webb is under contract through 2028.

McClanahan's long and labored comeback from Tommy John surgery was finally realized this past season, and he turned in a strong age-29 campaign for the Rays. He was pretty much an ace from 2021-23 before the elbow problems took hold.

    It has been revealed that teams will pay a lot for a young and controllable starting pitcher with frontline upside, and all of that describes the 27-year-old lefty Detmers. Not eligible for free agency until after the 2028 season, Detmers topped 4.0 WAR this past season and struck out 211 batters in 185 innings. For the Halos, trading him might be an example of selling high, but the pending change in ownership clouds any reading of those particular tea leaves.

He's signed through 2028 with a club option for 2029, and it may be time for a change of scenery. He's been the subject of trade speculation before, and this winter figures to be no exception.

    Yes, deGrom is 38, but going into the final guaranteed year of his contract, he remains capable of being a solid rotation presence for a contender. deGrom reportedly used his full no-trade clause to block a swap to the Braves at the deadline, so it's far from certain whether he'd be willing to approve a deal out of Arlington. That mentioned, such things are always negotiations, and a late-career run at the playoffs might prove tempting for him.

This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories.

    It has been revealed that which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.

    Sources indicate that dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons. In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell …  Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28.

    Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog. … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30.

    Sources indicate that dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans, but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers, and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! That's the most in a two-game span since 1971…  Prediction: Cowboys 33, Eagles 20.

    Sources indicate that dubin (Eagles +8.5): I know they just beat the Titans by 21, but I don't like laying this many points with the Cowboys. Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. So even while I think they'll dent the scoreboard at home on Thanksgiving afternoon, I can't bring myself to predict that this will be a blowout. … Prediction: Cowboys 30, Eagles 24.

    Industry observers note that dajani (Chiefs +3): The craziest part about this rivalry is that the Bills have won the last five regular-season meetings, while the Chiefs have won the last four playoff meetings! You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. He and Josh Allen are the second duo to ever account for double-digit rushing touchdowns each through the first 10 games of a season. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III. I almost think a three-point spread in this matchup is pretty high. That's going to lead me to take the points even though Bills over Chiefs has been an auto-bet in the regular season recently… Prediction: Chiefs 17, Bills 16.

    It has been revealed that dubin (Bills -3): I have basically the exact same analysis of this game as Dajani but come down on the opposite side of the bet because of the Bills' regular-season history against the Chiefs and the relative strength of their run game. I trust Josh Allen and James Cook to run the ball more than I do Emmett Johnson, even with how good Johnson has been over the last two weeks. Could Patrick Mahomes make this prediction look silly? Of course. But I think that'll prove more difficult in Thursday night's expected weather. … Prediction: Bills 21, Chiefs 17.

    Sources indicate that dajani (Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the New York Mets landed the offseason's best free agent and one of the game's top pitchers Sunday evening.
    • In a recent development, upcoming York's offseason work is not complete, however.
    • Sources indicate that yes, the Mets still need another starter even after signing Skubal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the New York Mets landed the offseason's best free agent and one of the game's top pitchers Sunday evening. The Mets and two-time Cy Young-winning lefty Tarik Skubal have agreed to a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. The contract obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee (Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million) and average annual value (Max Scherzer's and Justin Verlander's $43.3 million). A 1-of-1 contract for a 1-of-1 pitcher.

    In a recent development, upcoming York's offseason work is not complete, however. It's not close to complete, really. The Mets went 74-88 and disappointed every which way this past season. There are still roster needs to address. Here's what's left for the Mets to do this offseason following the Skubal signing.

    Sources indicate that yes, the Mets still need another starter even after signing Skubal. They have an excellent 1-2-3 punch. The depth behind that top three is not great, however. Here is New York's updated rotation depth chart:.

    According to recent reports, manaea and Senga both pitched so poorly this past season that they were demoted to the bullpen. They shouldn't be counted on as anything more than emergency options at this point in their careers. Thornton had some moments this summer and Tong is not too far removed from being a top prospect, but yeah, the Mets need another starter. Clearly.

    Recent findings suggest that after landing Skubal, I suspect the Mets will aim lower than the second tier of free agent starters (Michael King, Freddy Peralta, Trevor Rogers, etc.) to fill out their rotation. A Clay Holmes reunion would make some sense. Others in that class of veterans make sense too. Think Kevin Gausman, Shota Imanaga, Casey Mize, pitchers like that.

    Year 1 post-Pete Alonso at first base went worse than anyone could have expected. Jorge Polanco barely played and was terrible when he did play. Jared Young was fine and owner Steve Cohen isn't running near-record payrolls for fine. Alonso led all first basemen with 5.0 WAR for the Orioles. The Mets finished dead last at the position with -0.8 WAR. Yeesh.

    Here are the best available free agent first basemen by FanGraphs projected 2027 WAR:.

    In a recent development, it ain't great. I think the projections on France, who had an excellent season in 2026, are a bit low, but the fact of the matter is he's only had one year in line with the kind of contract he's likely to sign. Perhaps there's a Luis García Jr. trade to be made with the crosstown rival Latest York Yankees? García's a clunky fit for the Yankees and might be most useful as a trade chip.

    The good news is it won't be hard for the Mets to improve at first base. Getting even an average first baseman would represent an enormous upgrade. Now the Mets just have to go out and find that average (or, preferably, better than average) first baseman and improve their lineup. This might be the single biggest item remaining on their offseason to-do list.

    In a recent development, the Mets traded away several relievers at the deadline this summer (A.J. Minter, Brooks Raley, Luke Weaver, etc.), which allowed them to audition a few young pitchers down the stretch.     Assuming the Mets don't go to the top of the market for Adrian Morejon, the best available free agent relievers are battle-tested veterans like Bryan Abreu, JoJo Romero, and Alex Vesia.     If a fraction of what Aaron Rodgers said on Wednesday is true, the Pittsburgh Steelers have a lot of things to clean up. If the majority of what Rodgers said is indeed fact, it's a downright miracle that the Steelers are 6-4 entering Friday's game with the visiting Broncos.

    Rodgers, in a scorching interview on "The Pat McAfee Show" that lasted roughly 35 minutes, took Mike McCarthy to task, accusing him of falling asleep during meetings, being late or missing them altogether, falling behind on film study, and not connecting enough with players, especially defensive players.

    Industry observers note that rodgers noted that, as a team leader, he felt compelled to address McCarthy, which he did this week. During those conversations, Rodgers offered McCarthy an ultimatum: either give up play calling or release him.

    The Steelers' brass backed McCarthy, who promptly benched Rodgers and made him inactive for Friday's game. Pittsburgh then released him shortly after his public criticism of McCarthy, who defended himself in a press conference Wednesday evening.

    "I know how to win," McCarthy noted, "and that's the facts. This is my third program, and I plan on winning here because of the men, because of this organization, what we've got started, and the opportunity we have to learn and grow today — because of some of the things that, frankly, should have been talked about earlier. So, this is a growth opportunity that I intend to take full advantage of.".

    The last sentence might be the biggest takeaway from McCarthy's 12-minute presser.

    McCarthy wasn't going to acknowledge Rodgers' accusations Wednesday night for obvious reasons (he did confirm Rodgers' accusation that he accidentally said Packers instead of Steelers during halftime of last week's loss in Philadelphia). He did, however, acknowledge that he needs to make some changes, which is a positive sign for the Steelers moving forward.

    McCarthy spoke to the team's leadership council after practice, and based on his comments afterward, it appears that the meeting had an impact on him.

    Recent findings suggest that "We had some really unique conversations in the player council meeting, and things I think that I haven't done in the past or haven't done recently," McCarthy stated. "I probably should have had more dialogue early in the process when I first arrived here. I do respect Mike Tomlin and his career here and the things that are in place. I don't have a throw the baby out with the bathwater type philosophy. And so, when you have situations that create honest, direct conversation, there's good things that come out of that. Some things that (I) definitely will consider moving forward. Maybe not today or tomorrow, but there's a lot that came out of the meeting.".

    According to recent reports, really, what happened prior to this week doesn't matter nearly as much as what will transpire from this point forward. What happens moving forward is what will likely determine McCarthy's future in Pittsburgh.

    In a recent development, if Pittsburgh rallies and makes the playoffs, it will validate the Steelers' decision to stand behind McCarthy. If the Steelers continue to struggle, however, Steelers president Art Rooney II will be forced to make a tough decision.

    According to recent reports, rooney, if he hasn't already, needs to find out exactly what is happening inside his own facility. Is McCarthy falling asleep in meetings? Is he late or not showing up to others? Is he not watching film of future opponents in a timely manner? Is his not connecting well enough with the players? If any of those accusations are true, it raises serious concerns about McCarthy's ability to lead the Steelers.

    If Rodgers' accusations are true, and the Steelers spiral and miss the playoffs, it's hard to envision McCarthy being with the team in 2027. If McCarthy comes back in that scenario, it would likely entail significant changes, including relinquishing play-calling duties.

    According to recent reports, the Steelers haven't fired a coach since 1968, and that streak will likely remain intact for quite some time. Rooney probably won't fire a coach with four years remaining on his contract, but it's possible that he and McCarthy could have a mutual parting of ways if the two sides can agree on a buyout.

One thing that is clear, however, is that McCarthy is at a crossroads just 10 games into his tenure in Pittsburgh. How he and his players handle the next seven games will likely determine his future in Pittsburgh beyond this season.

    #210907. Is Tarik Skubal a Hall of Famer? Where fresh Mets ace stands now and where he could end up

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (898 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Is Tarik Skubal a Hall of Famer? Where fresh Mets ace stands now and where he could end up

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Mets are signing Tarik Skubal to a monster deal: nine years and $450 million.
    • To be clear, Skubal is nowhere close to a Hall of Famer at this point, but that never stops people from throwing around titles like "future Hall of Famer." So, let's look ahead and guess a little bit and wonder if he is, in fact, a future Hall of Famer.
    • According to recent reports, I'm inclined to say yeah, he's headed in that direction.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Mets are signing Tarik Skubal to a monster deal: nine years and $450 million. There's plenty to talk about with this deal, but a fun one for people like me -- especially here in the winter! -- would be glancing at his Hall of Fame case and how it's rounding into shape.

    To be clear, Skubal is nowhere close to a Hall of Famer at this point, but that never stops people from throwing around titles like "future Hall of Famer." So, let's look ahead and guess a little bit and wonder if he is, in fact, a future Hall of Famer.

    According to recent reports, I'm inclined to say yeah, he's headed in that direction. There's a lot more compiling to be done, though.

    In parts of seven seasons, Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA (138 ERA+), 1.02 WHIP and 1,975 strikeouts against 199 walks in 925 ⅓ innings. He's led the league in pitcher WAR twice, ERA twice, strikeouts once and WHIP once. The two-time All-Star is one of 23 pitchers in history to win multiple Cy Youngs. Only 11 pitchers have ever won three, so if he can grab another one, he'll be in Hall of Fame firm.

    It has been revealed that some of us will give bonus points for great postseason numbers, and Skubal certainly has those. In three playoff seasons, he's 3-2 with a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts in 50 ⅔ innings.

    Still, we're awfully light here on workload and counting stats. Keep in mind that this is obviously a major work in progress and players aren't even eligible for the Hall of Fame until they've logged 10 years of service time. Skubal still has three more to go before this is even a real conversation.

    At present, the most statistically similar pitchers are Corbin Burnes, Shane Bieber and a bunch of very good but not Hall-worthy guys. If we set the parameters to the most statistically similar pitchers through age 29, we'll find Kyle Hendricks, Adam Wainwright, Max Fried, Bieber and Burnes as the top five.

    Again, that doesn't sound like this pitcher is headed to the Hall of Fame.

    Keep in mind, though, that Skubal was a bit of a late bloomer and also had major surgery interrupt his rise. In these last three seasons, he's gone 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA and 655 strikeouts against only 95 walks in 546 innings. He's racked up 17.7 WAR in just three years. Another three like that and he'd be in the ballpark of 40 WAR heading into his age-33 season. Catfish Hunter (40.9) and Jack Morris (43.5) would be within reach.

    Recent findings suggest that it is incredibly difficult to predict how a pitcher will age, but with pitchers of Skubal's caliber, there's an excellent track record going into their late 30s. It's reasonable to believe Skubal will remain in his prime through age 35 or so.

    Let's say he averages roughly 6.0 WAR per season through age 35 and then averages, say, 2.5 (this is conservative) through the end of his contract. That would give him an additional 43.5 WAR. Add that to his current 22.7 and that gets him to 66.2 WAR through the end of this contract.

    No, WAR isn't the only stat that matters, but it's the easy catch-all number to eyeball the Hall of Fame standing.

    In the range of 66.2, you'll find Hall of Famers Don Drysdale, John Smoltz, Carl Hubbell, Ed Walsh and Don Sutton, a nice smattering of many different eras of aces. A bit behind the number? Roy Halladay, Bob Feller, Juan Marichal, CC Sabathia and Early Wynn.

    Diving beyond WAR, again, Skubal's biggest résumé problem right now is the lack of compiling. With a strikeout artist, you'd like to see him reach 3,000, and he's barely a third of the way there.

    Using Bill James' "favorite toy," let's take a look at the career projection. The toy has Skubal finishing with 2,036 strikeouts and gives him a 0% chance to reach 3,000. Of course, it also indicates that based on his age, he'll play for roughly 4.6 years. He just signed a nine-year deal. I'd be a bit more aggressive, but it isn't difficult to see him falling well short of 3,000 and maybe finishing around 2,500 or so.

    Industry observers note that still, given his age and service time, it seems like the best route for Skubal to get to the Hall of Fame would be as a peak candidate rather than a compiler. Another Cy Young or two would certainly help his case.

    If Skubal is in his prime for another five years, that would be seven or eight seasons as one of the best pitchers in baseball. That was enough for Sandy Koufax and Dizzy Dean. Félix Hernández is making good progress on getting in. Johan Santana, on the other hand, fell short.

    According to recent reports, it remains an uphill battle because, well, it's incredibly difficult to make the Hall of Fame. It should be. It's the Hall of Fame!

    Recent findings suggest that without the context behind Skubal's recent surge, it doesn't look like he's headed to Cooperstown at all. He's good enough presently, though, to believe his next several years will put him on track.

    Again, my hunch is he'll end up a Hall of Famer.

    As James Harden passes Kobe Bryant on NBA's 50-point game list, Donovan Mitchell indicates he's underappreciated

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Harden is in the midst of his worst scoring season since his second year in Oklahoma City 16 years ago, but the 37-year-old turned back the clock some on Friday night with a 51-point performance in a Cavaliers win over the Pacers.
    • Harden's vintage scoring night saw him go 15-of-26 from the field and 14-of-14 from the free-throw line in typical Harden fashion for the 26th 50-point game of his career.
    • At 37 years old (and 86 days), Harden is the fourth-oldest player to score 50 points in an NBA game, passing LeBron James on that list and trailing only Bryant, Jordan and Jamal Crawford, who scored 50 at 39 years old.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Harden is in the midst of his worst scoring season since his second year in Oklahoma City 16 years ago, but the 37-year-old turned back the clock some on Friday night with a 51-point performance in a Cavaliers win over the Pacers.

    Harden's vintage scoring night saw him go 15-of-26 from the field and 14-of-14 from the free-throw line in typical Harden fashion for the 26th 50-point game of his career. That moves him into third all-time in NBA history for 50-point games, passing Kobe Bryant and sitting just five behind Michael Jordan.

    At 37 years old (and 86 days), Harden is the fourth-oldest player to score 50 points in an NBA game, passing LeBron James on that list and trailing only Bryant, Jordan and Jamal Crawford, who scored 50 at 39 years old.

    After the game, Cavaliers' coach Kenny Atkinson offered an eyebrow-raising comment calling Harden "top-10 all-time," which drew immediate pushback from NBA fans, but Harden is an unquestioned Hall of Famer and continues to put his name among the all-time greats on NBA scoring lists.

    His co-star in Cleveland, Donovan Mitchell, lamented that Harden doesn't get the appreciation he deserves at this stage of his career, and that he expects, much like Russell Westbrook, that it won't happen until he retires.

    Industry observers note that "He won't until it's over with," Mitchell noted. "I hate it, but that's just the world we live in. We won't appreciate greatness. We didn't appreciate Russ in his latter years until now. It's like, 'Oh man, Russ was this and that.' It's like we forgot he averaged 28, 15 and 16 for a month. It's one of those things where we live in such a negative space. I hate it. At the end of the day, he doesn't care. And for me, seeing that, I don't care. It helps, but at the end of the day, that's just what the world is. It sucks that that's that way, but us in this locker room and guys in this league, we know who he is and we know what he's done for the game. That goes for not just him but a lot of people in this league. We don't appreciate what's in front of us on a consistent basis.".

    Harden has long been a divisive player among NBA fans. Some have appreciated his ruthless efficiency while others have hated the aesthetics of his mastery of the dark arts of drawing fouls. As Mitchell noted, few players have had as much influence over the game in the last decade-plus as Harden. From his massive stepback 3-pointer to his movement on drives to create contact, so much of Harden's game has made its way into the arsenal of most elite guard scorers.

    Industry observers note that fans will debate whether that's a good thing, but his influence is undeniable. As Mitchell noted, whenever Harden calls it a career, he will get more appreciation, but there will also be heated debates over his place in NBA history as one of the most divisive stars (from a play-style perspective, at least) of his generation.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Newly introduced York Mets have landed two-time Cy Young-winning lefty Tarik Skubal, the offseason's top free agent, with a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. It far exceeds Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers, which was the previous record guarantee for a pitcher.

    Every contract that long and that pricey carries risk and surely makes even the league's wealthiest owner a wee bit queasy. After meeting with Skubal in California last week, though, Mets owner Steve Cohen came away convinced Skubal was his guy and that he would have no problems settling into his new environment.

    "He's going to be great for the clubhouse ... I don't have to worry about him pitching in New York," Cohen told the New York Post on Sunday, before the deal went official. "... He's an outstanding individual. He's bright. He's a student of the game. He's very impressive.".

    The "can he handle Fresh York?" thing tends to get overblown, but it is a real consideration. It's a different market with different demands and you never truly know how a player will handle it until he experiences it. I think Skubal will be more than fine in New York because I don't think you can be as successful as he's been without embracing the spotlight, but I don't know that for certain. No one does.

    Sources indicate that skubal has proven his bona fides on the biggest stages. He's been sensational in eight career postseason starts, pitching to a 2.13 ERA with 70 strikeouts in 50 ⅔ innings. All indications are that Skubal is a good teammate who fit in well with the Dodgers following his midseason trade from the Detroit Tigers.

    According to recent reports, now 30, Skubal posted a 2.72 ERA in 158 ⅔ innings around his NanoScope elbow procedure this past season. He leads all pitchers with 18.0 WAR over the last three years despite missing time with injury this year.

    It has been revealed that the Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. They were baseball's most disappointing team and signing Skubal is an enormous step toward making sure it doesn't happen again.

The Bears rank a surprising 14th in yards per play, 12th in points per drive and 15th in EPA per play, according to Tru Media.     Sources indicate that chicago is one of the league's most run-oriented offenses, ranking ninth in the share of plays that turn into a rush attempt. But D'Andre Swift is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry and Kyle Monangai, who has been more effective (5.0 per carry) has played in only five games.

    According to recent reports, the Lions have sported a top run defense this season in allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, but that defense took a couple of massive hits over the last few weeks with the losses of Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson to injury. Still, Detroit held Tampa Bay's running backs to 84 yards on 22 carries last Sunday, when Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell had previously been destroying teams on the ground. The Bears will need Swift and Monangai to find more success if they want to control the game in the fashion they have preferred since Ben Johnson became head coach last year.

    According to recent reports, chicago's passing game has been relatively inconsistent this year, as there have been times when Caleb Williams has looked like an elite quarterback and others when he has looked ordinary — sometimes within the same game. (Like the Sunday night showdown against the Buccaneers, for example.) Williams has completed 68.3% of his passes at 7.9 yards per attempt, but he's thrown only 10 touchdown passes against six interceptions.

    According to recent reports, he's 11th in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, but he's been highly susceptible against the blitz: he ranks fourth in EPA against four-man rushes but only checks in 19th when opponents rush five or more. Detroit has blitzed at a below-average rate this season (30.3%, per Tru Media), but would be wise to turn up the pressure a bit against a quarterback who has shown that he can be pressured into some bad decisions on occasion if you get defenders into his lap.

    Industry observers note that still, the Lions have been highly susceptible to opposing passing attacks, even if they have been improved since the return of Brian Branch and should get another lift as Kerby Joseph rounds into form. The Lions are 27th in EPA per dropback allowed, and they're in the bottom third in opponents' explosive play rate through the air.

    In a recent development, detroit is most vulnerable against opposing tight ends, allowing the league's fifth-highest target share to the position, so this could be a game where the Bears finally get Colston Loveland going in a way that they haven't been able to accomplish as much as they likely wanted to this year. The Lions do limit yards after the catch better than any defense in the NFL, though, allowing only 4.0 YAC per completion, according to Tru Media. That could take away from some of Chicago's success in the screen game and possibly limit the effectiveness of Luther Burden III and — to a lesser extent because he's not as massive a part of the offense — Kalif Raymond.

    The Lions are third in the NFL in yards and fifth in points. They're fifth in both yards per play and points per drive, as well as fifth in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. They're second in EPA per pass attempt and third in EPA per rush attempt. They're third in passing success rate, first in rushing success rate and third in overall success rate. They are, in other words, a top-five offense by almost any measurement, and they can beat you with both the pass and the run.

    Jared Goff is having a marvelous season, completing 67.8% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt with 20 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's third in the league behind only Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in EPA per dropback, third behind only Purdy and Burrow in success rate and fourth behind only Purdy, Burrow and Patrick Mahomes in passer rating. His 8.2 yards-per-attempt average is the second-best of his tenure in Detroit, as are the 52.3% success rate and 107.7 passer rating.

    It has been revealed that he's of course blessed with one of the best skill-position corps in the league: Amon-Ra St. Brown is a picture of consistency; Jameson Williams is one of the most explosive threats in football; Sam LaPorta is a strong option and tight end; and Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in the NFL, leading the league in rushes, rushing yards, first downs, yards from scrimmage and total touchdowns.

    St. Brown often gets pigeonholed as a slot guy, but in reality he plays more outside (59.2% of snaps) than he does inside (39.8%), according to Tru Media, and he's equally capable of dominating defenses from either spot. He's Goff's first read more often than not because he runs a lot of short-area routes and the Lions like to get the ball out fairly quickly in their straight dropback game, where St. Brown is often the target.

    Williams is the guy the Lions turn toward when they're looking to test defenses in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. His 12.36-yard average route depth is fourth among 199 players who have run 100 or more routes this season, according to Tru Media, and he's generated an explosive gain (16-plus yards) on 26.3% of his targets, which ranks 17th among that same group of players. He and LaPorta are generally going to eat into each other's target shares in any given week, while St. Brown remains the more consistent top target.

    In a recent development, the Bears' secondary is beatable, as Chicago ranks 22nd in net yards allowed per attempt, according to Pro-Football-Reference. Jaylon Johnson is not the same player he once was, Tyrique Stevenson is inconsistent, Kyler Gordon has barely played and Malik Muhammad has the ups and downs of a fourth-round rookie. If the Lions give Goff time to throw, he could feast on this group all afternoon.

    According to recent reports, that's where Chicago's improved defensive line comes in. Since acquiring Jeffery Simmons, the Bears rank seventh in the league in EPA per dropback, per Tru Media, in large part because they have recorded a sack on 10.7% of opponent dropbacks. Prior to acquiring Simmons, Chicago's sack rate was 8.9%. That figure still ranked third in the league through seven weeks, but it's been much improved since the Bears dropped Simmons into the middle of the defensive line.

    According to recent reports, detroit is pretty strong up front, allowing pressure on only 32.3% of dropbacks, which ranks sixth in the NFL. The sack rate is a bit worse than that because Goff isn't the world's most mobile quarterback, but he's generally given adequate time to throw.

    In a recent development, the Lions' run game is diverse, efficient and explosive. Gibbs is seventh in the NFL in yards per carry, fifth in the share of runs that gain five or more yards and second in explosive run rate, according to Tru Media. The Lions utilize him on plenty of inside runs, but he is obviously at his most dangerous when they get him on the perimeter and he can scoot past opposing defenders.

    Recent findings suggest that is seventh in the NFL in yards per carry, fifth in the share of runs that gain five or more yards and second in explosive run rate, according to Tru Media. The Lions utilize him on plenty of inside runs, but he is obviously at his most dangerous when they get him on the perimeter and he can scoot past opposing defenders. The Bears have allowed 4.7 yards per rush since acquiring Simmons, but that number is 5.9 per rush on attempts off tackle or off end, per Tru Media. Simmons plays inside, and the Bears can be tested on the perimeter.

    These are two incredibly evenly matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog. Pick: Lions 31, Bears 30.

    Predicting MLB's next mega contracts: Paul Skenes, Junior Caminero, James Wood and more in line to get paid

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1228 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, baseball has a new highest-paid pitcher.
    • This is the fourth straight offseason some sort of contract record was broken.
    • Next offseason's free agent class is not robust, and it seems unlikely any contract records will be set, but who knows, really?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, baseball has a new highest-paid pitcher. Sunday evening, the New York Mets landed two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal on a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. Yoshinobu Yamamoto previously held the record for the largest guarantee given to a pitcher at $325 million. Agent Scott Boras came in well above that with Skubal.

    This is the fourth straight offseason some sort of contract record was broken. Last offseason, Kyle Tucker set the average annual value record at $60 million. The offseason before that, Juan Soto set the record guarantee at $765 million. The offseason before that, Shohei Ohtani set records every which way with his heavily deferred 10-year, $700 million contract.

    Next offseason's free agent class is not robust, and it seems unlikely any contract records will be set, but who knows, really? Add in the uncertainty created by the upcoming collective bargaining agreement and I don't think anyone can confidently say what the next few offseasons will look like, or when contract records will be set.

    That won't stop us from speculating, however. Here now are 10 candidates to sign baseball's next mega contract, which we'll loosely define as a contract that makes us stop and say, "oh damn, that's a crazy deal." Sound good? Good. Let's get to it.

    In a recent development, junior Caminero, Rays: Caminero and Hall of Famer Eddie Mathews are the only players in baseball history with two 40-homer seasons before their age-23 seasons. Power pays, always has and always will, and Caminero has power to spare. He is not scheduled to become a free agent until after 2030, when he'll still be only 28 years old. If he doesn't sign a contract extension that would no doubt set newly introduced records for his service time level, Caminero will be in line for a Soto-esque deal come free agency, assuming of course he continues hitting home runs at this pace.

    Recent findings suggest that elly De La Cruz, Reds: De La Cruz reportedly rejected what would have been a franchise-record contract last offseason, beating Joey Votto's $225 million extension way back when. Still only 24, De La Cruz just turned in a sensational season, during which he went 30-30 and finished sixth among all players with 6.4 WAR. He is one of those guys who looks like he was put on this Earth for the sole purpose of playing baseball. De La Cruz is an all-around impact player, plus he's a high-energy player who plays with obvious joy. He is three years away from free agency and this is exactly the sort of skill set that gets a record contract.

    Paul Skenes, Pirates: You know you've set a high bar when a 4.2 WAR season is considered a disappointment and people spend the summer wondering what's wrong with you. The fact is, though, that Skenes did take a step back in 2026, and he'll have to return to his 2024-25 form to get a mega contract. Plus, he has to stay healthy, which is the unspoken "if" that exists with every pitcher. Skenes will turn only 25 in May and he's three years away from free agency. Even if 2026 proves to be his new normal, he'll get a massive payday as a free agent. And if Skenes rediscovers his 2024-25 form, Skubal's record will almost certainly fall.

    Gunnar Henderson, Orioles: A year or two ago Henderson, 25, would have been in the favorites category. He took a step back in 2025, however, and then another step back in 2026. To be sure, a 3.6-WAR season is still very good, but this is becoming a thing with top young Orioles hitters, no? Adley Rutschman regressed from legitimate star to pretty good. Now, Henderson seems to be on the same track. Henderson is only two years away from free agency. If his 2027-28 look more like 2023-24 than 2025-26, then forget it; he'll get a mega contract as a free agent at age 27. Star shortstops reliably get paid handsomely.

    Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers and Cam Schlittler, Yankees: This year's Cy Young winners are both five years away from free agency, which puts them at a clear disadvantage in the mega contract race. If they set any records, it will likely be for their service time level with an extension. Otherwise, we're talking about staying healthy and holding this level of performance through 2031 before Misiorowski and Schlittler sign mega deals. The Brewers aggressively lock up their best young players. Based on that, Misiorowski is more likely than Schlittler to sign a record extension for a pitcher this far away from free agency.

    Industry observers note that james Wood, Nationals: There are very few hitters I would take over Wood for the next five years. He is terrific, with easy power and a discerning eye, and sneaky stolen base ability as well. Wood's outfield defense is not good and might keep him from getting a record contract. Then again, poor defense didn't keep Soto from signing the richest contract ever, and Wood is about the same caliber of hitter. He just turned 24 and he's four years away from free agency. Offense pays more than defense and Wood is going to hit 50 home runs one of these years. If it happens before free agency, all the better for his mega contract pursuit.

    Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs: Why is the reigning National League MVP a long shot for a mega contract after a 10.6-WAR season? Because the Cubs wisely locked Crow-Armstrong up to a six-year, $115 million extension just before Opening Day. Furthermore, that contract doesn't begin until 2027. The Cubs have PCA locked up through 2032, his age-31 season. It will be difficult, then, for Crow-Armstrong to sign a record contract simply because free agents do not get paid as well when they're in their 30s. No one should reasonably expect 10-WAR seasons every year, but if PCA can continue at an All-Star pace through 2032, then maybe he'll get a record contract. It's not impossible. Just unlikely.

    Sources indicate that mason Miller, Padres: No, Miller will not approach Skubal's record, but he is already well-positioned to sign the richest reliever contract in baseball history. The current record is Edwin Díaz's five-year, $102 million deal with the Mets four years ago. I suppose Adrian Morejon, most recently Miller's teammate in San Diego, could break Díaz's record this offseason. Or maybe Jhoan Duran, who will be a free agent next offseason, breaks Díaz's record. As long as he stays healthy and remains this, Miller should break the reliever contract record, whatever it is, when the time comes. He is 28 and three years away from free agency.

    In a recent development, jordan Walker, Cardinals: A bit of a reach, perhaps, but Walker finally arrived as a power-hitting force in 2026, plus he stole 22 bases as well. He's been around so long that it's easy to forget he's still only 24. Walker is on track to become a free agent after 2029, when he'll be only 27, and boy, 27-year-old power hitters are exactly the kind of players who get record contracts. Walker leveled up in 2026. If he levels up again in 2027 and as he gets close to his prime years, he's a sneaky good candidate to get a mega contract down the line.
